DirectX 9.0c SDK (August 2005): headers and import libraries
============================================================

from    dxsdk_aug2005.exe (md5 053c7a32ce3d7982eb1191863d4e2ddb,
        https://archive.org/details/dxsdk_aug2005), unpacked with 7-Zip without
        running the installer. The outer self-extractor holds dxsdk.exe, whose
        payload holds Include/, Lib/x86/ and Documentation/License Agreements/
        (the EULA, copied to License/). Every file listed below is
        byte-identical to that payload.

Why this SDK
------------
A compatible reconstruction input, not the exact build input. game.dat imports
d3dx9_27.dll, the D3DX runtime this release introduced, and this release's
Include/d3dx9core.h defines D3DX_SDK_VERSION 27. Nothing in game.dat names the
SDK build its units were compiled against.

game.dat also imports dinput8.dll. It imports no d3d9.dll or dsound.dll
(Direct3DCreate9 is reached at run time), so d3d9.lib and dsound.lib are not
vendored. d3dx9.lib is an import library only (327 import members and the
d3dx9_27.dll descriptors, no code objects): the D3DX bytes in game.dat come
from the inline functions of d3dx9math.h/.inl, compiled into game units, never
from a static library. dxerr9.lib, the one static DirectX library game.dat
links, is vendored separately in vendor/dxerr9-aug2005/.

Use
---
A source opts in with a `// dxsdk` line (tools/build.py source_needs_dxsdk):
Include/ is then searched before every path the unit names, so SDK
declarations come from these headers, never from a stand-in under
reference/shims/. tools/dx_migration.py classifies the units that still use
a stand-in (reverse/dx_migration_queue.tsv).

Before such a unit compiles, tools/build.py checks every file row below: a
missing or different file, or a file in Include/ not listed here, stops the
build. There is no fallback to the stand-ins. .gitattributes keeps this
directory -text, so every checkout holds the bytes hashed here.

License
-------
Microsoft Software License Terms, DirectX 9.0 Software Development Kit Update
(August 2005): License/DirectX SDK EULA.txt, verbatim.
